goal: Make embedded harnesses safely self-update with three-way reconciliation and make routine command-line operation a first-class harness capability.

alignment.evidence: v0.5 work is isolated on athena/harness-lifecycle-v0.5 and PR #6 is stacked on the unmerged v0.4 PR #5 so lifecycle changes remain independently reviewable.

The v0.4 handoff contract, generated-project state, VCS controller, skill router, engineering defaults, Git merge primitives, package history, and regression failures from PR #6 were inspected and used to drive the implementation.
00-PLANNING/SYSTEM-MODEL.md confirms managed lifecycle inputs/outputs, baseline state, three-way update flow, CLI capability, failure boundaries, invariants, and evidence.

Lifecycle operations do not force push, push managed work to main/master, merge, deploy, release, mutate production, spend provider credits, store credentials, or perform sudo/root/system package changes.

HARNESS-MANIFEST.json owns the managed surface; .harness/baseline and handoff.json own installed lifecycle state; harness-update.js owns doctor/adopt/update; vcs-control.js owns ordinary Git actions; product planning/state/source remains project-owned.

The slice adds only the manifest, baseline/handoff lifecycle state, doctor/update/adopt controller, command-line skill/routing, generated-project handoff changes, documentation/ADR, and focused regressions needed for safe upgrades.

The updater remains zero npm runtime dependency on Node 20+ and Git, uses Git's native three-way merge, refuses unknown baselines and real conflicts, preserves removed/project-only files, and avoids a second orchestration framework.

PR #6 Actions run #25 passed on Node 20, 22, and 24 after lifecycle updater, CLI discovery, legacy adoption, conflict handling, and generated handoff regressions were repaired; every job passed npm test, npm run control:verify, and npm run memory:resume. Final documentation/state reconciliation remains covered by the same PR CI gate.
